DATE:  October 21, 2020

TO:  Arts Commission

FROM:  Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department

SUBJECT: Love, Inglewood Public Art Collection Purchases
________________________________________________________________

RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended the Arts Commission recommend the City Manager approve
purchases totaling $11,860 for 11 unframed works on paper directly from eight
professional Inglewood artists, to be separately framed and professionally installed in
public areas as the Love, Inglewood portable public art collection.

BACKGROUND
Portable public art collections are comprised of original artworks created for display on
public walls and pedestals. Inglewood has a suite of signed artist’s prints purchased in
the 1970s and displayed in City Hall. The Senior Center collection is comprised of
paintings and small sculptures purchased from the 2017 Inglewood Open Studios.

Love, Inglewood will be the third portable art collection and reflect the work of
contemporary Inglewood artists. The City used a three-step process to identify artists.

Nineteen Inglewood cultural art workers, artists working on City contracts prior to 2020
and former Art Commissioners nominated 28 artists who were each invited to apply by
submitting up to three, two-dimensional works on paper, 24 x 24” or smaller, and made
with permanent, museum-quality materials, with a purchase price of up to $1,500 for
each work, including Inglewood’s 10% sales tax and scheduled delivery to City Hall, and
appropriate for all audiences. These parameters guide the artists and inform art framing
and installation budgets.

Twenty-one nominated artists submitted 59 art works they felt suitable for City facilities,
totalling $67,220. A panel of contemporary art experts from civic, educational and
museum institutions reviewed the submissions in an online process and ranked each
work for purchase. The panelists were:
   Paul Baker-Prindle, Director, Kleefeld Museum of Contemporary Art, California
  State University, Long Beach, and visual artist;
   Sharon Garrett, Inglewood Economic Development Department Manager, and
  ceramics artist; and
   Kali Nikitas, Communication Arts Department Chair, Otis College of Art and
  Design, former Inglewood Arts Commission Chairwoman and designer.

  One W. Manchester Boulevard • Inglewood, CA • 90301 • Phone (310) 412-8750 • Fax (310) 330-5750 •
  www.cityofinglewood.org
 Rating each artwork through Calforentry.org, the national online image management
service, the jurors found consensus and recommend purchase of the following 11
artworks on paper by eight artists, at the following prices:

  Sharon Barnes*  The Straphangers  1,000
  Kelly Brumfield-Woods  Lidar and All Night Fireball  2,200
  Martin Durazo  Sprinkles and Earth  3,000
  Charles Fine  Elemental Forces 2  1,500
  Gale McCall  faces  760
  Lindsey Nobel  Planetary Awareness  1,300
  Minna Phillips  Alternate Series #5  1,200
  Megan Riera  Randy’s in Line 1 and
  Long Front Blue White Thread  900
  Eight Artists  Eleven Artworks  $11,860

The purchases total $11,860 which includes Inglewood’s 10% sales tax and City Hall
delivery for each. Prior to acceptance and processing an artist’s invoice, a final
inspection of the physical artwork will be made by staff to ascertain condition and
permanence.

DISCUSSION
Inglewood artists are hard hit by the pandemic and subsequent cancellation of events,
exhibitions, teaching contracts, workshops, and residencies. The Love, Inglewood
program recalibrates Inglewood Growing Artists Projects (IGAP) 2020 to provide
support and recognition of our most respected artists through purchases and display.
City facilities are currently closed to the general public. This provides time for purchased
artworks to be safely received then professionally framed. The artworks will be installed
with identification plaques, in well-lit, publicly accessible, high-trafficked areas of city
facilities. Siting decisions will be made in conjunction with the City’s facility managers.

FISCAL IMPACT
Funds for this agreement are available in account code 055-070-7010-44870 (Public Art
Fund, Contract Services).

*Inglewood artist Sharon Barnes has no relation to the Director of Parks, Recreation and Community
Services Department Sabrina Barnes.

Presented by: Sabrina Barnes, Director Parks, Recreation and Community Services

minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, October 21, 2020 via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf called
the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

  Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Absent
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the minutes from September 16, 2020. Commissioner
Banks seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Banks, Ehrlich-Bell and Lesure
  Nays: None

Special Presentation

Elsje Kibler-Vermass, Los Angeles Philharmonic Vice President for Learning, Youth Orchestra Los Angeles (YOLA),
YOLA National and YOLA Beckmen Center gave an overview of the history and services provided by YOLA. YOLA
provides children in under resourced communities with free high-quality instrumental education and academic
support. YOLA is now in its 14th season and has become one of the country’s most influential music education
programs. YOLA is non-profit and a community resource providing young people ages 5 through 18 with after school
music instruction up to 12 to 18 hours per week, academic tutoring, leadership training and opportunities to perform
in their communities and on stages around the world. YOLA extends beyond music, it’s about developing the whole
child. In doing so, YOLA can also be seen as a creative youth development program. Currently there are four (4)
sites in Los Angeles making Inglewood the fifth site, the first to be situated at its own dedicated home.

The Beckman YOLA center is designed by Architects Frank Gary and Learning Help for All YOLA at the Inglewood
City Hall campus. Opening in early 2021 and is the next step in YOLA’s evolution, serving about 350 to 500 students
from the neighboring community annually starting with about 150 students in year one (1).
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Inglewood City Hall campus will also be the home of the YOLA institutes, providing leadership development and
pre-professional training opportunities. It will also serve as a rehearsal and performance space bringing together
students from all of YOLA’s sites to play together and functioning as an International Teaching Center, hosting
teacher trainings and convenings for music educators from the U.S. and around the world. The venue will serve as a
Community Space by opening the doors of the center to musicians and community groups in and around Inglewood.
The building’s redesign will still consist of the original exterior walls while shaping into a beautiful space. The new
facility will have a large performance space with the capability of converting into two small multi-purpose spaces
divided by a moveable acoustic wall. Additional rehearsal and practice rooms will circle the buildings perimeter and
include spaces for choir, sectionals and individual practice. The facility will have fiber optic cables which will support
distance learning and videoconferencing.

The YOLA Inglewood Program is for students from Inglewood and will first and foremost reflect the demographics of
the City of Inglewood. The enrollment guidelines will follow the best practices. Year one (1) in 2021 will focus on both
early elementary students with no musical experience and also beginner to immediate level string students to help
jump start the future program growth. The YOLA program will be the first to be launched at the Beckman Center.
Construction should be complete by the start of 2021.

Commissioner Lessure asked who are the proposed instructors, teachers and administrators for this particular site?
Ms. Kibler-Vermaas stated everyone will be brand new to the site. YOLA is currently hiring for a Director and once
that position is filled, the Director will begin to hire staff locally and in the surrounding cities. Commissioner Lessure
stated there is a lot of local talent. Where will you be posting this information or will you be waiting to hire the Director
first? Ms. Kibler-Vermaas said we are waiting to hire a Director but we are open to any recommendations. We are
new to Inglewood and are open to learning from others where to post the information and be able to tap into the
Inglewood artists and teachers.

Helen Lessick asked when you speak about community involvement how much community involvement do you
mean? Ms. Kibler-Vermaas stated we are trying to get familiar with the new space and interested in listening and
having conversations with others. We have a beautiful space that we would love to share with others. The space will
be designed specifically for the music and the arts. Commissioner Lessure asked Moses Aubrey to share his
experience with YOLA. Mr. Aubrey stated YOLA is great because it really has a sense of community within the
program, nothing compares to YOLA and what they have to offer as far as funding, programs and teachers.

Commissioner Lesure asked Mr. Aubrey if he thought YOLA was the catalyst for him to go on to UCLA and learn how
to play a double bass and a music major? Mr. Aubrey stated absolutely, if it wasn’t for YOLA he would have never
went to UCLA or earned a degree. Commissioner Lesure stated it is very important to hear the wonderful
accomplishments of YOLA students and is looking forward to being in touch.

Commissioner Ehrlich-Bell asked how many students the program will start with. Ms. Kibler-Vermaas stated in the
first year, we will start off with150 students and at year five (5) hope to be at capacity (450-500 students). The
program is high intensive 5-days a week, starting off with the younger students in hopes of growing the program.

Commissioner Metcalf shared her excitement and thanked Elsje Kibler-Vermaas for her presentation.
  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

Staff Report

Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the City Manager
approve purchases totaling $11,860 for 11 unframed works on paper directly from eight (8) professional Inglewood
artists, to be separately framed and professionally installed in public areas as the Love, Inglewood portable public art
collection. Helen Lessick gave an overview of the staff report which included the selection panel process and
selection. Commissioner Lesure asked what the average amount of money the artists will receive for their work. Ms.
Lessick stated the artists set their own price but the cap was $1,500.

Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Banks seconded and the staff report
was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Banks, Ehrlich-Bell, and Lesure
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports Regarding the following Public Art Related Projects

  None

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  None

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:58 p.m.
